subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What should OpenClaw treat as an allowed protected config mutation path when an agent, plugin cron, or host exec command can invoke the CLI?
rationale: This is a security-policy boundary rather than a single narrow bug: current source has a guarded gateway config tool, a separate CLI path available through host exec, assistant-visible repair hints, and plugin cron behavior claimed by the reporter.

options.title: Require operator provenance for protected writes
options.body: Keep operator CLI writes available but add a guard or provenance rule so agent, plugin, or cron-origin protected config writes are refused or surfaced for explicit approval.

options.title: Only remove assistant-facing hints
options.body: Treat message hardening as the first mitigation, while keeping this issue open or splitting follow-ups for CLI-through-exec and memory-core provenance.

options.title: Document current trust model
options.body: Document that agents with host exec authority can run the CLI and mutate config, and close the behavior as expected after updating docs and security guidance.

recommendation.title: Require operator provenance for protected writes
recommendation.body: Keep operator CLI writes available but add a guard or provenance rule so agent, plugin, or cron-origin protected config writes are refused or surfaced for explicit approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox/exec UX and security posture, and history shows repeated work on the affected sandbox and exec diagnostic surfaces.
